children: CrowdStrike (CRWD), the cloud-native endpoint and identity-security company, faced fresh pressure Tuesday as Palo Alto Networks pushed deeper into continuous AI-powered security testing. CrowdStrike shares slipped to $247.82. Palo Alto's new Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense continuously probes web applications, APIs and cloud infrastructure for weaknesses, then recommends remediation that can include code-level fixes and virtual patching.

That puts another heavyweight directly into the race to automate more of the security workflow. CrowdStrike is not entering that fight empty-handed. Its latest quarter ended with annual recurring revenue of $5.84 billion, up 25% year over year, while net new ARR reached $332.8 million. The Falcon platform also stretches across endpoint, identity, SaaS, cloud and network security, giving CrowdStrike a broad installed workflow from which to push additional AI-driven products.

The real contest is moving beyond endpoint protection toward discovering exposures, deciding which threats matter and fixing them with less human intervention. CrowdStrike's advantage is the security data and operating workflow already concentrated inside Falcon, but Palo Alto is attacking the same consolidation opportunity from another direction. The valuation leaves little room for disappointment: the picture shows CrowdStrike at $247.82 versus a GF Value estimate of $136.97, meaning the stock trades 80.93% above GF Value. That premium makes customer consolidation especially important to watchinvestors are already paying heavily for CrowdStrike to remain one of the platforms absorbing more of the cybersecurity stack.

title: CrowdStrike Slips as Palo Alto Automates Vulnerability Hunting
